nuggets.title: New users see blank home feed

scenario.symptoms: Day-0 retention dropped after launch in a new country. Users with no click history received empty recommendation responses because the ranker returned 404 when collaborative features were missing.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Serving path requires user embedding from training; no fallback to popular or content-based lists for cold users.

incident.headline: Serving fails closed when collaborative features are absent

agenda.goal: Deliver relevant items for cold-start and sparse users.
agenda.opener: New users got an empty feed—how should cold start work in this recommender?

evidence.strong: Layered fallback: geo/popular, content-based from signup prefs, explore/exploit, smooth transition as events arrive.
evidence.weak: Require historical embedding or return empty.

probes: How quickly should personalization kick in after first clicks?
What signals exist at signup before any events?
hints: Cold start is a product requirement, not edge case.
agenda.referenceFix: Serve locale/popular and content-based defaults on embedding miss, blend scores as interaction count grows, and monitor empty-response rate.

scenario.symptoms: Home feed p99 latency hit 800 ms after expanding candidate retrieval from 200 to 10,000 items. Ranker GPU queue backed up while ANN search stayed fast.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Architecture retrieves huge candidate sets synchronously before ranking; no early termination or cascade.

incident.headline: Oversized candidate set overwhelms ranker on the critical path

agenda.goal: Meet feed latency while preserving recommendation quality.
agenda.opener: Feed got slow after retrieval widened—how do you balance recall and latency?

evidence.strong: Multi-stage retrieval with tight top-N, lightweight pre-ranker, parallel ANN shards, caching, and dynamic candidate limits under load.
evidence.adequate: Bigger GPU fleet without reducing candidates.

misconceptions.pattern: Believing more candidates always improves quality without cost.
misconceptions.challenge: Who pays GPU time to score 10k items per request?

probes: What is the right N before heavy ranker?
hints: Cascade: cheap retrieval then expensive rank.
agenda.referenceFix: Retrieve hundreds not thousands via ANN + filters, pre-rank to ~200 with lightweight model, GPU-rank top slice, and degrade candidate count when queue latency rises.

nuggets.title: New model ranking worse in production

scenario.symptoms: Offline AUC improved 8% but online CTR dropped after deploy. Training logs used imputed defaults for missing features while serving returned null and a different imputation path.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Feature pipeline for batch training and online serving diverged after a refactor touched only the batch job.

incident.headline: Training and serving feature logic diverge causing skew

agenda.goal: Keep training and serving features consistent.
agenda.opener: Offline metrics improved but online CTR fell—what skew issue could cause that?

evidence.strong: Shared feature definitions, feature store with point-in-time correctness, training-serving validation tests, and shadow scoring.
evidence.weak: Separate ad-hoc batch and serving code paths.

probes: How do you test serving features against training snapshots?
hints: One source of truth for transforms.
agenda.referenceFix: Centralize transforms in feature store, run parity tests between batch export and online fetch, and block deploy when distribution drift vs training set exceeds threshold.
